text:
Network requests fail. Servers time out, connections drop, and overloaded services return errors for requests that would succeed a moment later. Retrying is the obvious fix, but a hand-written retry loop is easy to get wrong and tedious to repeat across a codebase.

This library handles retries for you. When an HTTP request fails, it tries again using exponential backoff, so the wait between attempts grows after each failure and a struggling server has time to recover. Jitter adds a random offset to each delay. That keeps many clients from retrying at the same moment and hitting the server all at once.

The library has zero dependencies. Installing it adds nothing else to your environment, so you have no version conflicts to resolve and no extra packages to audit.

The current release is version 0.9, and the test suite covers 94% of the code. Because this is still a pre-1.0 release, the API may change before 1.0. Bug reports and feedback are welcome. If you hit an edge case the library doesn't handle, please open an issue so we can cover it before the stable release.
